Scheduled actions (Automations and System Automations)

Schedule work to run unattended — fleet changes an operator plans (Automations) and the product's own housekeeping such as backups, syncs and probe sweeps (System Automations) — fired by a dedicated scheduler service.

What is it?#

A scheduled action is an entry from SATOM's automation catalog, bound to a set of target appliances and a schedule. A separate background service — the scheduler — fires each action when it is due and records the outcome in a run history.

The catalog is split over two pages that share one table:

  • Automations (Automation → Automations) — fleet work an operator plans: a cutover, a drained backend, a certificate swap or renewal, an upgrade preparation, a firmware upgrade, a reboot, an HA failover, a Custom REST call.
  • System Automations (Administrator → System → System Automations) — SATOM maintaining itself: backups, source-of-truth syncs, probe sweeps, report building, signature and CVE refreshes.

❗Important — Nothing is scheduled until the first appliance

No scheduled action is created by the installer, the database setup or a service start. When the node gets its first appliance, SATOM creates the default set of System Automations (see Seed the minimum set). Until then — or after you deleted every System Automation — the node has zero coverage (no backups, no syncs, no monitoring sweeps) while looking perfectly healthy.

ℹ️Note

Changed on 2026-10-14: System Automations moved to Administrator → System. Upgrade preparation, firmware upgrade, reboot, HA failover, the certificate renewals, the Cert Manager lifecycle sweep and Custom REST call moved from System Automations to Automations, so operators can schedule them; existing rows of those actions now appear on Automations. Automations is live in the Global, FortiWeb, FortiADC, FortiAnalyzer and FortiAuthenticator ADOMs. SATOM now creates the default System Automations when a node gets its first appliance. A bound row runs only if its change request covers it.

What does it do?#

  • Offers the catalog of automatable operations (below), cut to what the current ADOM's appliances support.
  • Fires each enabled action on its schedule: once, interval, daily, weekly, monthly or cron.
  • Runs an action against the selected appliances, or against every appliance of the kinds the action supports when no target is selected.
  • Skips appliances in maintenance on automatic runs (a manual Run now still reaches them).
  • Keeps a per-action Run History with status, trigger, summary and log.
  • Refuses to fire firmware upgrade, reboot, HA failover, the Cert Manager lifecycle sweep and Custom REST call unless they are bound to an approved change request that covers them, inside its maintenance window.

Requirements#

  • satom-scheduler.service must be running on the primary node. Only that service fires actions; the web workers never do. On a standby the service idles until the node is promoted.
  • At least one registered appliance for actions that need targets.

Permissions#

Page Permission Who has it by default
Automations (/web/automations/) any key that grants the legacy config_write, typically operations.apply Operator, Administrator
System Automations (/web/scheduled-actions/) users.manage Administrator
  • Without the permission the sidebar entry is hidden and the URL answers 403.
  • Each page only opens rows of its own kind. Asking the Automations page for a System Automation by id answers 404, so an operator cannot edit or delete the nightly backup through the page they are allowed to use.
  • The page a row lives on follows its action's catalog, not the row: a row created on System Automations before an action moved to Automations now appears on Automations.
  • Rows are also scoped to the ADOM they were created in; a row from another ADOM answers 404.
  • The Automations entry is live in the Global, FortiWeb, FortiADC, FortiAnalyzer and FortiAuthenticator ADOMs, and greyed out with the reason in the FortiGate ADOM.
  • Operators can schedule every Automations action, but upgrade, reboot, HA failover, the Cert Manager lifecycle sweep and Custom REST call run only bound to an approved change request. Approving a change needs users.manage.

How to use#

Create an automation#

  1. Open Automation → Automations (fleet work) or Administrator → System → System Automations (housekeeping) and press New Action.
  2. Name — free text, e.g. Nightly config backup.
  3. Action — pick from the catalog. The line below shows its Scope: and, for destructive actions, "Destructive — handle with care." For upgrade, reboot, HA failover, Cert Manager lifecycle sweep and Custom REST call it also shows "Runs only bound to an approved Change Request, inside its maintenance window."
  4. Targets — Ctrl/Cmd-click one or more appliances, or leave it empty to target every appliance the action supports ("Leave empty to target the whole FortiWeb fleet." — the action's own product list applies).
  5. Advanced params (JSON, optional) — the inputs an action reads (see Configuration). For Custom REST call a dedicated Custom REST request card replaces this box.
  6. Schedule — choose the Frequency and its fields (see below).
  7. Tick Enabled ("eligible to fire on its schedule") and, if wanted, Catch up ("run a missed fire instead of skipping it"). Both are ticked by default.
  8. Press Create action. The flash reads "" created.

Schedule kinds#

Frequency Fields Notes
Once Run at (date and time) Wall-clock time in the console timezone (the label names the zone). Fires one time, then has no next run. Locked for upgrade, reboot and HA failover: "This action is locked to a one-time (once) schedule."
Interval Every n minutes / hours / days A duration, counted from the end of the previous fire; unaffected by daylight-saving changes
Daily Time of day Wall-clock time in the console timezone
Weekly Weekday & time (Monday … Sunday) Wall-clock time in the console timezone
Monthly Day of month & time (1–31) Day 31 in a 30-day month fires on the last day
Cron Cron expression (5 fields) minute hour day-of-month month day-of-week: *, lists, ranges, /step, month and weekday names, Sunday as 0 or 7; when both day fields are restricted a day matches if either does. Wall-clock time in the console timezone. An expression that is invalid or can never fire (30 February) is refused on save

All wall-clock fields — Run at, daily, weekly, monthly and cron times — are read in the timezone set under Settings → General and stored as UTC. The Next run column on the list is shown in that same timezone, with its zone.

ℹ️Note

Changed in 2.11.0: Run at is now read in the console timezone (it used to be taken as UTC and fired off by the timezone offset), Next run shows its zone, and a fire skipped while the scheduler was down shows as missed.

Run, disable, edit or delete#

On the list, each row offers:

  • Run history (list icon) — every run with Started, Finished, Status (ok, failed, skipped, running), Trigger (schedule or manual), Summary and Log.
  • Edit (pencil).
  • Run now (play) — asks "Run '' now? This executes synchronously against the live target(s)." The page waits for the run and then flashes Run finished (): .
  • Enable / Disable — enabling recomputes the next run from now.
  • Delete — also deletes the action's run history.

Filter the list with Name contains…, Any action, Any status (enabled / disabled) and Any schedule, then Filter. Tick Remember for me to save the filter on your profile (one saved filter per page); Clear forgets it. Showing N of M is always displayed because a hidden automation still fires. A user who holds both permissions also gets Also show , which lists the other page's rows read-only with an Open button to the page that owns them.

Seed the minimum set#

Automatically. When a node gets its first appliance, SATOM creates the default set below — the same plan as sudo satom execute seed actions. The Appliance created message counts the System Automations it created. This happens only while the node has no System Automation at all: if one exists, the set is left as the administrator left it, and rows you deleted are not re-created.

By hand. The command still fills individual gaps. On the primary node, as root:

sudo satom execute seed actions          # shows the plan, changes nothing
sudo satom execute seed actions --yes    # creates the missing rows

Existing rows are never touched — a row matching the same action and schedule kind is left alone, even if you renamed it. The command refuses to run on a standby. Confirm afterwards with sudo satom diagnose scheduler or sudo satom get scheduler status.

Created as Action Schedule
Hourly fleet sync (source of truth) device_sync every 60 minutes
Nightly SoT snapshot + off-box push (all devices) device_inspect daily 02:45
Nightly system backup (Postgres + JSON -> server) system_backup (push to server on) daily 01:30
Deep monitors + Service Monitor — probe sweep deep_monitor every 3 minutes
Fleet metrics — scrape to the local store metrics_scrape every 3 minutes
Daily monitoring report monitor_report (daily, mail, push, keep 90) daily 02:00
Weekly monitoring report monitor_report (weekly, mail, push, keep 53) weekly Monday 02:10
Monthly monitoring report monitor_report (monthly, mail, push, keep 36) monthly day 1, 02:20
Sentinel — correlate and score sentinel_sweep every 3 minutes
Sentinel — recompute behavioural baselines sentinel_baseline daily 03:10
Sentinel — refresh the local CVE mirror sentinel_vuln_sync daily 03:30
Daily inventory snapshot (Metrics trend) inventory_snapshot daily 23:50
Knowledge packs — check the feed, download, import knowledge_fetch (3.0) daily 04:20
Signature DB freshness — read each FortiWeb's version signature_check (3.0) daily 06:15

A node updated from 2.x has neither of the two 3.0 actions until you run the seed (or create them by hand): no update creates scheduled actions.

All seeded rows — automatic or by hand — are System Automations, enabled, with catch-up on.

Configuration#

The catalog — System Automations#

Key Label Targets Notes
backup Config backup FortiWeb On-device configuration backup
device_sync Sync device to local source of truth all four products Read-only full config read into the local cache
device_inspect Sync device + push SoT off-box all four products Sync, then upload new blobs to the external backup server
deep_capture Deep capture (full policy/WPP tree) FortiWeb Read-only, one box at a time
signature_sync Sync signature database FortiWeb Refreshes the shared signature catalog
signature_check Signature DB freshness — read each FortiWeb's version none 3.0. One read-only CLI read per FortiWeb; the catalog is re-read only when a version changed; stale or unreadable databases raise a device alert. See Signature freshness
knowledge_fetch Knowledge packs — check the feed, download, import none 3.0. What it does depends on the fetch mode (off, notify, download, download_import); primary only. See Knowledge packs
system_backup System backup (Postgres + JSON) none push_server (default on) uploads the bundle
git_bundle Git repository backup (bundle) — retired none Still runs manually; never seeded
deep_monitor Deep monitors — probe sweep none Feeds both Deep monitors and Service monitor; schedule every 3 minutes
artifact_refs WAF artifacts — refresh the policy→artifact index none Bounded per run; daily is enough

sentinel_baseline Sentinel — recompute behavioural baselines none Nightly; touches no appliance
sentinel_vuln_sync Sentinel — refresh the local CVE mirror none Refuses to run unless the CVE sync setting is on
sentinel_feed_publish Sentinel — expire blocklist entries and mirror the list none Every 15 minutes suggested
monitor_report Monitoring report — period summary none period (daily/weekly/monthly), email, push_server, keep
stats Build statistics summary none No device call
appid_import Import AppID catalog (nightly) none Additive import from the configured URL
inventory_snapshot Record inventory snapshot (daily counts) none Daily, for trend comparisons
health_check Health check (system status) FortiWeb Read-only
ha_check HA status check FortiWeb Read-only
cert_scan Cert Manager — scan device certificates FortiWeb Daily; feeds the Certificate Manager

The catalog — Automations#

Key Label Targets Notes
policy_set_status Enable / disable a server policy FortiWeb, one appliance policy, enabled (true/false)
backend_set_status Enable / disable a backend (pool member) FortiWeb, one appliance server_pool, member, enabled
backend_set_config Change a backend's IP / port FortiWeb, one appliance server_pool, member, ip and/or port
swap_certificate Swap a server-policy certificate FortiWeb, one appliance policy, certificate
upgrade_prep Upgrade preparation (backup + health) FortiWeb, FortiADC Destructive flag. Stores a citable pre-upgrade run
upgrade Firmware upgrade (FULL - flashes + reboots) FortiWeb Requires a change request. Once only. See note below
reboot Reboot the appliance (DESTRUCTIVE) all four (FortiWeb implemented) Requires a change request. Once only; reason (max 100 chars)
ha_failover HA failover - hand the primary role over (DISRUPTIVE) FortiWeb ≥ 8.0.0, FortiADC ≥ 7.6.0; one target Requires a change request. Once only; direction set / unset
cert_manager_server Cert Manager — renew Server certs FortiWeb Generate, sign, deploy under a new name; no binding swap. Also a change-request type
cert_manager_clientserver Cert Manager — renew Client+Server certs FortiWeb As above
cert_manager_client Cert Manager — renew Client certs FortiWeb As above
cert_lifecycle Cert Manager — lifecycle sweep (revoke + cleanup) FortiWeb Destructive. Requires a change request. Reports only unless auto-apply is on
custom_rest Custom REST call FortiWeb Destructive. Requires a change request. Method, endpoint, mkey, JSON body
run_process Walk a process every product; one walk per target Destructive flag (so never through the generic actions API). process (the process key), armed (off = rehearsal). An armed walk of a diagram that writes runs only bound to an approved change request. See Process

The four server-policy and backend actions go through the same snapshot + audit + change-history path as a manual edit, and act on the first selected appliance only. Requires a change request means the row runs only bound to an approved change request that covers it, inside its maintenance window (see Change-request binding under Advanced).

⚠️Warning — The scheduled firmware upgrade does not flash in this release

When an upgrade action fires inside an approved window it reports "Firmware upgrade for is not executed by the headless service layer (no upgrade runbook); no firmware was flashed." and the run is graded failed. Flash firmware from the appliance's Upgrade page inside the approved window — see Putting an appliance under change control.

Custom REST request card#

Field Description Required Example
Method GET (read only, body ignored), POST (create), PUT (update), DELETE Yes PUT
Endpoint A registry key or an /api/... path; start typing to search Yes /api/v2.0/cmdb/server-policy/policy
mkey (object name, optional) Object name for writes No pol-demo
JSON body (POST / PUT) A JSON object; anything else is ignored with a warning No {"status": "disable"}
Label (optional) Shown in run summaries No Disable a maintenance banner

Writes go through the snapshot + audit + dry-run path. The firmware partition-boot endpoint is refused outright because it reboots the box even on GET.

Example#

🧪Example — Drain a backend for a Saturday maintenance

On Automations → New Action: Name Drain app-02 Saturday, Action Enable / disable a backend (pool member), Target fweb-01, Advanced params {"server_pool": "pool-app", "member": "2", "enabled": false}, Frequency Once, Run at 2026-11-07 22:00 (console timezone). Create a second action with "enabled": true for the restore. Both appear on the Calendar.

Result#

  • Each fire writes a run row and updates Last status (ok, failed, skipped) and Next run on the list. A fire rolled forward without running because the scheduler was down and Catch up is off shows Last status missed.
  • An automatic run whose targets are all in maintenance is skipped, not failed: "
  • An action with no matching appliance is skipped: "No matching appliance."
  • Create, edit, enable/disable, delete and Run now are written to the audit log (scheduled_action.create, .update, .toggle, .delete, .run_now).

Troubleshooting#

"This action is already running — try again shortly."#

Possible causes — the scheduler (or another Run now) holds the action's run lease.

Solution — wait for the current run to finish and check Run history. A lease held longer than 60 minutes is reclaimed automatically (see Advanced).

"change request: before the maintenance window" (status skipped)#

Possible causes — the action is bound to a change request whose window has not opened, has closed, is not approved, or is waiting for external approval.

Solution — open the change request; fix its window or approval and press Re-schedule. See Change requests.

"

Possible causes — you created an upgrade, reboot, HA failover, Cert Manager lifecycle sweep or Custom REST call action by hand on Automations, so no change request is bound to it. The form cannot bind one: only the change request's Schedule button does.

Solution — raise a change request for the action instead.

"change request #N authorizes 'X', not 'Y'" / "change request #N does not cover device id(s) …" / "change request #N authorizes named devices; this action targets the whole fleet" (status skipped)#

Possible causes — the row is bound to a change request that does not cover it: the change authorizes another action, or the row targets devices the change does not name, or the row targets the whole fleet while the change names devices. The change request is left untouched.

Solution — use a change request that names this action and these devices: raise it, have an administrator approve it, and press Schedule on it.

"“

Possible causes — wrong page, wrong ADOM, or a target of a product the action does not support.

Solution — follow the page named in the message, switch ADOM, or deselect the named appliances.

Nothing ever runs#

Possible causes — no rows exist (a node with no appliance yet, or every System Automation was deleted), the scheduler service is stopped, or this is the standby node.

Solution 1. sudo satom diagnose scheduler — reports whether anything is firing. 2. sudo satom execute seed actions --yes on the primary if the list is empty. 3. sudo satom get service status scheduler to check the unit.

Verification — Last status shows a recent value and the run history grows.

"Advanced params were not valid JSON and were ignored."#

Solution — re-open the action and fix the JSON; the action was saved with empty params.

Advanced#

Advanced How the scheduler fires

satom-scheduler.service ticks every 45 seconds. Each tick first reclaims stale leases, then fires every enabled action whose next run has arrived. A fire claims the action with an atomic database update (running_at), so an action runs exactly once even if Run now is pressed at the same moment. The lease is always released when the run ends; a lease held longer than scheduler.lease_ttl_minutes (default 60) is reaped, the dead run is recorded as failed with "Lease reaped: …", and the action fires again on its normal schedule.

Catch up. When an action is overdue and Catch up is off, a fire that is more than 5 minutes late (for an interval: more than three intervals, at least 5 minutes) is rolled forward without running and its last status is set to missed — so a node that was off for a week does not fire a week of backups at once.

Advanced Change-request binding

An action carrying change_request_id in its params is authorised by that change request at fire time: approved/scheduled/in progress, external approval on record if required, and now inside the window. The change must also cover the row: the same action, and only devices the change names. A row for another action, for a device the change does not name, or for the whole fleet when the change names devices is skipped with the reason, and the change is left untouched. On success the change request moves to in progress and is closed from the outcome (ok → completed, anything else → failed).

Only the change request's Schedule button writes change_request_id; the form can neither set nor remove it. These rows are named CR #<id>: <title> (with - round i/n when the rollout is split into rounds) and live on the page of their action's catalog — Automations for upgrade, reboot, HA failover and the certificate renewals.

Advanced Data stored
  • scheduled_action — name, action key, scope, product (ADOM), targets (list of ids; empty = all), params (JSON), schedule kind and JSON, enabled, catch-up, next/last run, last status, lease.
  • scheduled_action_run — one row per fire; summary capped at 500 characters, log at 8 000.
  • Per-appliance progress rows are written as each device starts and finishes; they are shown on the Upgrade Flow execution page.
  • An action whose key is no longer in the catalog stays scheduled; each fire is recorded as failed ("Unknown action …"). The list marks it unknown action on System Automations — edit or delete it.
